subject: Transportation Systems
title: Tunnel Boring Machines
description: A 60-second lesson on Tunnel Boring Machines.

hook.text: A tunnel boring machine is a factory on wheels. It eats rock at the front and installs walls behind.

buildup.text: The rotating cutter head grinds through soil or stone while hydraulic rams push the machine forward.

discovery.text: Behind the cutter, workers bolt concrete ring segments into place. The tunnel appears as it goes.

twist.text: TBMs cost up to $100 million each. Most are custom-built for one project and never reused.

climax.text: A good TBM can advance 50 feet a day underground without disturbing a single building above.

punchline.text: The machine digs, builds, and moves—all at once.

quiz.question: What does a tunnel boring machine do behind its cutter head?
